answer.rationale: Memory c1 shows the incumbent has been stable across two renewal cycles with no integration disruption—critical given the 94% utilization with no buffer and the 14-day clock. Memory c6 shows multi-year commitments with the incumbent unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope, which is the lever I need to hit the 18% spend reduction without changing suppliers. I want both verified before committing: c1 confirms delivery risk stays flat under renewal, and c6 confirms the incumbent will actually move on unit cost for a longer term rather than just holding price. If either verification changes my read—e.g., c1 shows a recent service slip or c6 shows the volume-tier only applied at higher spend than I'm committing—I'll pivot to negotiate_terms. I am not choosing switch_primary_vendor (c2's onboarding speed is real but migration risk with 14 days and no buffer is unacceptable) or add_second_source (c3's value is structural, not a same-cycle cost lever) or defer_decision (c5's month-to-month posture doesn't survive a hard expiry in 14 days).
